atr.method: arithmetic mean of last 20 closed true ranges including signal bar

protective_execution: Normal/stress assume predeclared protective orders can react inside each 4h bar. Stop gap fills at the adverse open; favorable target gaps receive only the target price. If both stop and target are touched, stop executes first. New brackets are active after entry; no reentry after any exit on the same bar. Intrabar fills have an interval, not a fabricated precise timestamp. No tick data, volume queue or intrabar jumps are modeled.
entry_policy: Frozen M30 episode admission and optional confirm3, using only closed data. Entry only at first rising edge of the admitted target; signals observed while holding are not entered late after an RR exit. No leverage, averaging down or additional entries.
stop_updates: Breakeven and trailing updates use only a post-entry closed bar available before execution, with the same configured lag. Breakeven activates after that close is >= entry fill + initial ATR risk distance. Cost-adjusted breakeven includes entry/exit fees and modeled slippage. Trailing = max(old stop, prior close - 2*prior ATR20).
partial_exit: Sell floor-to-lot 50% of initial quantity at 1R and remaining quantity at 3R; move remaining stop to cost-adjusted breakeven only after the partial bar closes and update latency elapses. If a partial is below venue minimum, keep the whole position for 3R without activating breakeven. On ambiguous bars stop precedes all targets.
sizing: Allocation is a fraction of available cash. Risk is a fraction of account equity divided by the expected per-unit loss at the initial stop including fees/slippage, capped by available cash. Risk is nominal and can be exceeded by gaps/late execution. Quantity floors to 0.00001 BTC; minimum quantity 0.00001, minimum reference notional 1 USDT; current LBank limits are historical assumptions.
rr_definition: Configured RR is the gross price-distance reward multiple; report net planned RR and realized average win/loss separately. Fixed bracket is anchored to actual modeled entry fill.

selection.profit: Training 10000 only: maximize stress PnL; require normal PnL >= baseline and stress PnL >= 1.05*positive baseline stress PnL (or positive if baseline nonpositive), and worst normal/stress DD <= 1.10*baseline worst DD; ties use listed order; otherwise baseline.
selection.efficiency: Training 10000 only: maximize min(normal CAGR,stress CAGR)/max(normal DD,stress DD). Require positive stress CAGR, normal CAGR >= 0.75*positive baseline normal CAGR, worst DD <= baseline worst DD and score >= 1.10*positive baseline score; otherwise baseline.
selection.evaluation: Report profit-pick success only when evaluation normal/stress PnL >= baseline and worst DD <= 1.10*baseline; efficiency success requires evaluation score >=1.10*baseline, normal PnL >=0.75*baseline and normal DD <=0.80*baseline. Never retune after inspecting evaluation. Baseline fallback is not a new improvement.

robustness: Both-target ordering sensitivity is diagnostic only for the two training-selected candidates and baseline. Main results always use stop-first. Check prefix invariance, independent Decimal ledger replay, original baseline equality and partial-fill accounting.
data: Reuse the hash-verified 8514-bar Bybit frame and 672-bar LBank frame from the prior study. The invalid long LBank intake stays excluded; no repaired/imputed/dropped candles and no new exchange requests.
classification: Retrospective structured parameter search of 27 predeclared paths. This history was already observed in prior studies; time splits and anchored walk-forward constrain this run but are not pristine unseen-data qualification. Overlapping windows and model runs are not independent market samples. No automatic Paper change.
